heatmap.title: Dynamic Heatmap
description: This view shows where movement has accumulated up to the current frame. Green areas indicate lower-risk movement density, yellow areas are in the middle, and red areas indicate higher-risk movement density. Use this view to observe how movement builds over time and whether certain body regions are repeatedly active.
compareWithNormal: Compared with normal infant movement, infants with cramped-synchronized movements may show more rigid and repetitive heatmap patterns, with multiple joints becoming active together rather than moving in a relaxed, spontaneous, and varied way.

lineplot.title: Dynamic Individual Lines
description: This view shows one line for each selected joint up to the current frame. The line rises when that joint is moving more strongly at that moment. The magnitude is scaled relative to the movement observed up to the current frame. Choose Speed to see how much the joint moves from frame to frame. Choose Acceleration to see when the movement changes suddenly. Compare the line shapes to see which joints are more active and when.
compareWithNormal: Compared with normal infant movement, infants with cramped-synchronized movements may show multiple joints activating and relaxing together. In these periods, the line patterns for several joints may appear similar in shape.

stackedlineplot.title: Dynamic Stacked Lines
description: This view shows the movement of all selected joints together in one shared graph across the full sequence. Each colored line shows how movement for one joint rises and falls over time. Values are scaled relative to the movement observed so far across all selected joints. A line rises when that joint is moving more strongly at that moment. Use this view to compare joints directly. When multiple lines rise at the same time, those joints may be moving together. When one line stays much higher than the others, that joint is contributing more movement at that time.
compareWithNormal: Compared with normal infant movement, infants with cramped-synchronized movements may show multiple joints activating and relaxing together. During these periods, the line patterns for several joints may appear similar in shape, although they may not fully overlap because movement magnitude can still differ across joints.

episodes.title: Dynamic Movement Episodes
description: This view represents only detected strong movement episodes as bars for each selected joint up to the current frame. Wider bars indicate longer movement episodes, while taller bars indicate stronger movement. The episodes are redetermined using a threshold that updates as the video progresses, using only the movement up to the current frame. As more frames become available, a bar may appear, disappear, return, or merge with nearby bars. Choose Speed to detect episodes when the joint is moving strongly from frame to frame. Choose Acceleration to detect episodes when the movement changes suddenly. Compare the bars to see which joints have stronger, longer, or more frequent movement episodes, and whether multiple joints become active at similar times.
compareWithNormal: Compared with normal infant movement, infants with cramped-synchronized movements may show multiple joints activating and relaxing together. In this view, bars for several joints may appear and disappear at similar times, with similar widths and heights.

componentvariance.title: Dynamic Component Variance
description: This view shows how different joints contribute to each movement component extracted from the recording. A component represents an important or repeated movement pattern in the body. Click a component to show that pattern in the movement visualization on the left.

For each joint pair, bars extending to the left and right of the center line compare the left and right joints. Longer bars indicate that the joint contributes more to that component. The percentage shows the joint's relative contribution, with all joint contributions adding up to 100%. Joints contributing more than 40% are marked with an exclamation point.

Use this view to see whether that pattern looks balanced across both sides or leans more toward one side. Because this is a dynamic view, the contribution values are calculated using only the movement observed up to the current frame. As you move through time, you can watch whether the pattern stays even or becomes more focused in a few joints.
compareWithNormal: Compared with normal infant movement, infants with cramped-synchronized movements may show more components dominated by one joint, such as a single joint contributing more than 40%. This may indicate that the movement pattern is less evenly distributed across the body.

heatmap.title: Static Heatmap
description: This view shows the total movement accumulated across the full sequence for each selected joint. The vertical line across all plots indicates the current frame shown in the movement visualization on the left. Green areas indicate lower-risk accumulated movement, yellow areas are in the middle, and red areas indicate higher-risk accumulated movement. Use this view to compare when movement starts to build and which joints show the greatest overall activity.
compareWithNormal: Compared with normal infant movement, infants with cramped-synchronized movements may show a more gradual and aligned buildup of movement across joints, suggesting that multiple joints are becoming active in a more synchronized pattern.

The vertical line across all plots indicates the current frame shown in the movement visualization on the left. The episodes are determined after seeing the entire recording, so this view shows the strongest movement episodes across the full sequence. Choose Speed to detect episodes when the joint is moving strongly from frame to frame. Choose Acceleration to detect episodes when the movement changes suddenly.
